title: Checklist or steps
use_cases: Use when performing a developmental editing audit of a manuscript
Configure when establishing a character profile during early-stage workshops
Implement when troubleshooting a character that lacks agency or narrative drive
Use when evaluating the role and necessity of secondary characters in a scene
Implement when refining dialogue to ensure a distinct character voice
content:
The following elements form a functional character-construction audit sequence used across workshops and developmental editing contexts:

1. Core desire identified — the character has a specific, active want (not a passive state)
2. Internal vs. external goal distinguished — surface goal and psychological need are articulated separately
3. Misbelief or fatal flaw named — a specific false belief or dominant flaw shapes behavior
4. Contradiction present — at least 2 traits that create internal tension are operative
5. Agency demonstrated — the character makes at least 3 meaningful choices that change the story's direction
6. Reaction pattern consistent — the character's responses under pressure align with established psychology
7. Voice distinct — the character's dialogue and thought patterns are distinguishable from every other character
8. Arc type defined — growth, fall, or flat arc is intentional, not accidental
9. Backstory used sparingly — the manuscript contains less than 20% of total backstory developed in notes
10. Secondary characters serve the protagonist — each supporting character illuminates or complicates the central conflict
